beats.text: Everything in K-Desktop starts with a {command}command: a list of actions, in order, that runs when you press its hotkey.
Let's {build}build one from start to finish, look at {actions}every kind of action, and see all the ways to {launch}launch it.
On the Commands page, click {new}New command, and give it a name: {name}Work mode.
Next, a hotkey. Press any combination: {ctrl}Control, {alt}Alt, {w}W.
A hotkey can also be a {mouse}mouse button, like Mouse 5. A {chord}chord of two buttons, like Mouse 4 plus left click. Or the {wheel}wheel with a modifier, like Control plus Wheel Up.
Now, the actions, in order. {run}Run application: Notepad. {wait}Wait one second. {window}Window: left half. {volume}Volume: twenty percent. {folder}Open folder: Documents.
Press {ctrl}Control, {alt}Alt, {w}W... and it {all}all happens, in order, in a fraction of a second.
Each action can be {test}tried on its own, {copy}copied, {move}moved up or down, or {off}switched off for a while, without deleting it.

And every command gets an icon {auto}automatically. Or you pick one: {symbols}any Windows symbol in {colors}fifteen colors, {winicons}Windows icons, your own {images}images, or a {favicon}website's own logo.
Add action opens the catalog: {count}more than fifty actions, in {ten}ten families, with a {search}search box on top.

{apps}Open and run: programs, folders, web pages and scripts. {windows}Windows: place them, keep them on top, or restore a whole layout. {input}Keyboard and mouse: keys, text, the clipboard and macros.

{sound}Sound: volume, devices, music and recording. {screen}Screen: screenshots, video, copying text, a magnifier, a ruler and a colour picker. {network}Network: web requests, Wake on LAN, sending to your phone, mail and Telegram.
Then {calendar}calendar events, the {system}system's power and files, the {flow}flow, like messages, waits and other commands, and finally, the {assistants}assistants' own.
Besides keys and buttons, a hotkey can be a {corner}corner of the screen: just rest the mouse there.
Or a {gesture}mouse gesture. Hold the right button, draw a {letter}letter or a line, and let go. You can even {own}draw your own.

And without a key at all: from the {menu}QuickMenu or the {launcher}launcher, by {voice}voice, from your {phone}phone, from {network}another computer, a script or Home Assistant, from an {event}event, or by asking an {assistant}assistant.

Each command has its own options, too. Limit it to {apps}certain applications: if the same hotkey exists for {every}every app and for {one}one in particular, inside that app, the {wins}specific one wins. {block}Block the key so the app never sees it. Add a {sound}sound, {notes}notes, and extra {phrases}phrases to call it by voice.

K-Desktop runs as {admin}administrator, so its hotkeys work even over {elevated}elevated windows. But {each}each action decides whether its program starts as {asadmin}administrator, or as your {user}normal user.

One last tip: the {if}If action. It checks something first. Is a {program}program open? What {time}time is it? Is a {device}device connected? How busy is the {cpu}CPU? When the answer is {no}no, it {stop}stops the command, or {skip}skips the next actions. So one command can take {paths}different paths.
Next up: {next}the QuickMenu and the launcher.
Thanks for watching.
